### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via TursoDriverConfig (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8cdbe0c6e5af61613749f22105c03652fc0f4043` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9b4415682fd9b39647ff0dd1b4a986f4e8f3e37e` — the merge of head `7052b91110cbaea15fdb07422ed4f3af41f8afb0` into base `8cdbe0c6e5af61613749f22105c03652fc0f4043`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9b4415682fd9b39647ff0dd1b4a986f4e8f3e37e && git checkout 9b4415682fd9b39647ff0dd1b4a986f4e8f3e37e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8cdbe0c6e5af61613749f22105c03652fc0f4043 7052b91110cbaea15fdb07422ed4f3af41f8afb0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8cdbe0c6e5af61613749f22105c03652fc0f4043 && git merge --no-ff 7052b91110cbaea15fdb07422ed4f3af41f8afb0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8cdbe0c6e5af61613749f22105c03652fc0f4043
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8cdbe0c6e5af61613749f22105c03652fc0f4043` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2242ad5138d6a7857b54f576d06784196124b991`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #20200 (body and all six comments — triage 5854158738, unblock 5854953310, claim 5868842793, report 5869079328, amended claim 5869128452 as the surface and rulings, report 5870627032); #19977 (body, ten comments); rider #20437 (open); PR #20447 (body, nine-file list, net diff against merge-base `87c37aec1`: 9 files, +328/−29, head is a true merge of `origin/main` into the branch's three commits); the check-runs on the head, read last. No worktree, build, test, gate or ablation. Byte-equality of the two constants was checked by comparing the source literals from `git show` as text in the scratchpad — no project code was run.

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. `new TursoDriver` refuses `syncUrl` under a forced `mode: 'remote'` — RIGHT. The predicate is `mode === 'remote' && config.syncUrl` with `mode = detectMode(config)`; with `syncUrl` truthy and no forced mode `detectMode` answers `replica` for every url class (:1649, :1669, :1678), so only a forced remote reaches it, exactly as the PR body and the constant's docblock say. Placed after the three existing refusals and before `super()`, so no already-refused configuration changes message. Ruling 1's shape.
2. `sync` with no `syncUrl` refused in every mode — RIGHT. `config.sync && !config.syncUrl`; an empty `syncUrl` is unset by the same truthiness `detectMode`, `connect()` (:1819) and `sync()` (:3447) read and the spec's own refinement (`cfg.sync && !cfg.syncUrl`) applies. The seat's planned decision 1, accepted in 5869128452.
3. Nothing the parity table holds as accepted is refused — RIGHT. The control (forced remote, no `syncUrl`), a `file:` replica beside `syncUrl`, `sync` beside `syncUrl` under a forced `mode: 'local'`, an empty `syncUrl` alone, and the rider (`file:` + `mode: 'replica'`, no `syncUrl`, no `sync`) all still construct: table rows :92–:101 at head and the new file's CONTROLS block pin them. The rider plus `sync` is refused on the `sync` key, not the rider, consistent with #20437.
4. The two constants are byte-equal to the schema's issue texts — RIGHT, verified: `REMOTE_MODE_SYNC_URL_REFUSAL` (362 chars) equals the spec's and the mirror's `syncUrl` literal; `SYNC_WITHOUT_SYNC_URL_REFUSAL` (178 chars) equals the spec's `sync` literal. The `SYNC_KEY_REFUSALS` pin (8 rows) holds them against the BUILT spec dist; its own verdict is Test Core's.
5. The reworded spec clause ("the turso driver refuses this configuration when it starts") — TRUE for the constructor since this diff and TRUE as the schema's statement about the driver; the rest of the message is byte-identical (the two hunks are the same two lines); the mirror's dormant copy follows. The `sync` message is reused unchanged and stays TRUE. Ruling 2 delivered.
6. The D3 entry edit — TRUE: `buildTursoDriverConfig` forwards `syncUrl`, `sync` and `mode` unparsed (:169–:206), the entry is semantic so no conversion rewrites a row, and the constructor now refuses both shapes at boot. `registry.ts`'s hunk is byte-identical to the entry's: generator output only. No copy of the old sentence survives anywhere at head (git grep: 0 hits).
7. `not-required (already-registered turso-config-transport-mismatch-refused)` — HONEST. The gate verifies only that the id resolves and pre-dates the base (it does: PR #20199 at `172b4cf30`, before `87c37aec1`), never coverage. Judged on content: the entry is this family's, its `replacement` already names the same three ways out the changeset's FROM → TO table gives, and its `acceptanceCriteria` ("re-save every turso datasource ... the driver builds from it") already prescribes what a stored row needs at boot; this diff adds the boot half to its `reason`. `registered` would be false (no new id) and `no-migration-prescription` is refused by the body's own FROM → TO block.
8. Public surface — none moved: no export added in either package, `TursoDriverConfig` keys unchanged; the `syncUrl` / `sync` TSDoc extensions are TRUE; `check:api-surface` rides Lint & Repo Gates (success).
9. H4 readings — TRUE at head: `default-datasource-driver-factory.ts:1337` builds the real driver; `DatasourceConnectionService` records `failed-degraded` with `datasource 'NAME': connect failed — REASON` (:936); a test connection answers `Failed to build driver: ...` (`datasource-admin-plugin.ts:707`); ADR-0062 D5's fail-fast set (bound objects, external `onMismatch: 'fail'`, `bootCritical`) shares `OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE`.
10. Blast-radius sentences — TRUE: `isSyncEnabled()` has no caller outside `driver-turso` (only the changeset names it); the only `.sync()` outside is sqlite-wasm's own handle; no example, template, skill or doc authors either shape (grep of `mode: 'remote'` and `syncUrl` across `examples`, `templates`, `skills`, `content`, `docs`). One imprecision in the PR body: "the one downstream real-driver construction is dogfood's `:memory:`" — dogfood also constructs `{ url: 'libsql://test-db.turso.io', authToken }` (`date-bucket-parity-turso.test.ts:144`); neither carries a sync key, so both are untouched. Harmless.
11. Parity-table sentences — TRUE by count at head vs merge-base: 59 vs 55 rows (four `sync` rows added), 18 vs 16 forced-mode rows (the 18 mirror skips: 16 plus the two new forced-mode `sync` rows), `inert` 0 vs 4; the floors (`syncUrl` ≥ 3, `sync` ≥ 5, sync-key refusals ≥ 8, `inert` exactly 0) are as the PR says.
12. Every other changeset and PR-body sentence checked reads TRUE, with one FALSE: the Acceptance note "Comments that still describe the pre-change behaviour sit in fenced files" is FALSE for the driver mirror `src/spec/turso.zod.ts` — that file is in the amended claim's surface and in this diff (its :260–:265 hunk); it is TRUE for the spec copy ("nothing else in `packages/spec`"). The README is outside the listed surface but under no ⛔. Carried to ③.
13. Acceptance note, pre-existing and not moved by this diff: for a config with two defects (`sync` with no `syncUrl` beside a refused url, e.g. a remote url under `mode: 'local'`) the schema's first issue is on `sync` (the `superRefine` runs that check before `tursoTransportIssues`) while the constructor refuses on `url` first. No table row spells it; both doors refuse. Noted, not this card's.

Check-runs on `2242ad513`, final read 2026-09-28T13:28:46Z: 33 runs — 26 success, 3 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), 0 failed, 4 IN PROGRESS: Test Core (1/6), Test Core (3/6), Test Core (5/6), Type Check · workspace. Required contexts: Lint & Repo Gates success (carries `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:migration-registry`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:api-surface`); Build Core success; Dogfood Regression Gate success (all three shards); Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL) success; Governed Surface Queue Guard success; Test Core in progress (shards 2, 4, 6 success; 1, 3, 5 in progress); Type Check · workspace in progress. The two families NOT MEASURED locally: `check:type-check-debt` → Type Check · debt ledger, success; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` → Build Core, success. This record does not vouch for the in-progress runs: the byte pin and both packages' suites land in Test Core, and the landing waits on those shards and the workspace type-check.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/driver-turso`: `minor` with the BREAKING banner — RIGHT. An accept-set narrowing on the published constructor, shipped `minor` under the launch-window convention (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` header), bang in the title, `check-changeset-no-major` green on the head.
- `@objectstack/spec`: `patch` — RIGHT. Message text only, one `reason` sentence in a registered entry, and the regenerated registry; no accept set, key or export moves.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — RIGHT and the TRUE answer: nothing widened, nothing added or renamed; the value is identical on the changeset and on the PR body's second line, both copied from claim 5869128452; `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and the changeset says so. Not `skip-changeset`.
- FROM → TO for a stored pre-#20199 row: three rows plus the paragraph that names the boot consequence (`factory.create` throws, `failed-degraded`, `ok: false` on test, ADR-0062 D5 fast-fail, the `OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE` hatch), the before-behaviour and the way out — sufficient. It does not name the edit door (Setup → Datasources, the datasource admin service); the entry's acceptance criteria does. Adequate.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (report 5870627032, PR body), each answered:
1. Deviation, `packages/spec/src/data/driver/turso.test.ts` — TRUE (one title, one `toContain`; 2 lines) and minimal: the mechanical consequence of ruling 2, without which the spec suite reds. Accepted.
2. Deviation, `turso-driver.ts` outside the constructor body — TRUE and minimal: two constants (ruling 1 prescribes them), a 7-line `refuseIgnoredSyncKey` in the envelope shape `refuseSuppliedClientTimeout` already uses, and two TSDoc extensions that read TRUE. Accepted.
3. The rider stays — answered: filed as #20437 (open, read), pinned as accepted by the new test, reason given in the PR body and the changeset. Matches ruling 3.
4. `open_questions`: none in the delivering report; round 1's A/B was ruled A in 5869128452 and A is what landed (module constants, parity pin, no spec export).

The three carriers, judged:
- (a) `driver-turso/README.md` constructor-refusal list — NOT made FALSE. That list is scoped to the local-engine refusals (its lead sentence: the local and replica modes run through a local SQLite engine, "the constructor therefore refuses"), its config snippet already says `sync` "(requires syncUrl)", and no README sentence claims a sync key is ignored. Incomplete, not false; not owed in this PR — a docs follow-up in the dev's package.
- (b) The comments beside `tursoTransportIssues` in both copies ("What the driver refuses at construction, or constructs and ignores" — mirror :393, spec :470) — made FALSE by this diff: with `inert` pinned at exactly 0, the driver constructs-and-ignores nothing the schemas refuse. The mirror's copy is in a file this diff edits and inside the claim's surface — it should be fixed in this PR; the spec's copy is fenced by "nothing else in `packages/spec`", so its fix is the seat's call, though ruling 2's rationale (text must be true) reaches it. Same class, same files, not declared by the dev: spec `turso.test.ts:199–:201` "(which it constructs and ignores)"; the D3 entry's header comment ("together with the one combination the driver builds and then ignores") and its `reason`'s present-tense "One more it builds and then ignores: syncUrl under a forced remote mode ... Nothing the constructor accepts is refused, that key aside", eight lines above the corrected sentence and contradicting it in tense (the "#19977." dateline makes it readable as history; an upgrade-guide reader gets both); the mirror's section heading :85 "refuses or ignores". ESCALATED to the seat: reword in this PR (four comment lines and two clauses of ledger text, the entry being already in the amended surface as "text only"), or carry as a filed note. None is a TSDoc, changeset or PR-body sentence and none is runtime text; the verdict does not turn on them. The PR body's "sit in fenced files" (①.12) is FALSE for the mirror and should be corrected when the body is next edited.
- (c) `service-datasource`'s `turso-driver-config.test.ts` key-list case (`mode: 'remote'` + `syncUrl` + `sync: {}`, :68–:85) — NOT made FALSE: it pins key forwarding only ("exposes exactly the keys it can emit") and asserts nothing about validity; its first case already spells a shape the constructor has refused since #19893. Correctly left alone: the package is ⛔ in the claim. Acceptance note, as filed.

1.    Residual grep over the diff's 8 hand-written files at the new head for `constructs and (then) ignores`, `builds and then ignores`, `refuses or ignores`, `accepts and then ignores`, `that key aside`, `arm aside`: 0 hits.
